newsitem.title: CHAD: Chad president names southerner as prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Chad president names southerner as prime minister.

text.p: Chad's president, Idriss Deby, has named a senior member of his ruling party as prime minister following the resignation of Djimasta Koibla and his government, presidency officials said.

Nassour Guelengdoussia Ouaido, who has served in previous governments as minister of education and of planning and cooperation, and in the influential post of secretary general at the presidency, is a southerner like his predecessor.

His appointment followed a decision by Deby's southern rival, General Wadal Abdelkader Kamougue, on May 8 to rally to the president in the name of national unity. Koibla and his government resigned on Friday.

Presidency officials said the new government would include members of Deby's Patriotic Salvation Movement (MPS), Kamougue's Union for Renewal and Democracy (URD) and outgoing foreign minister Saleh Kebzabo's National Union for Development and Renewal (UNDR).
All three agreed earlier to form a joint government.
Deby's party won a 63-seat absolute majority in parliament in January and February elections. Kamougue's party came second, picking up 29 seats.

Parliament elected Kamougue speaker of the 125-seat national assembly on May 9. "I have accepted to manage the country with President Idriss Deby to preserve democratic gains, unity and peace in Chad, which is still a fragile country," Kamougue said after rallying to Deby.

Deby, a former guerrilla leader from the Moslem north, seized power in a 1990 French-backed coup after decades of civil war or conflict with Libya. After repeated electoral delays, he won a multi-party presidential poll in July.
Chad, one of the world's poorest countries, has discovered significant reserves of oil in the predominantly Christian south and north of Lake Chad.
The government has reached preliminary agreement with foreign oil companies on exploiting the oil and also envisages a pipeline to a sea terminal in Cameroon. Chad is landlocked.
